subject: How can one "capture" warnings from INLA?

messages.author: 2d1c0edfe132eb41
messages.subject: How can one "capture" warnings from INLA?
parts:
Dear INLA team/INLA users,

I am using INLA for the analysis of microarray data looking for differentially expressed genes. This implies that I am fitting a model about 18,000 times (to different genes).

I have noticed that if I fit the model to a list containing the gene intensities using "lapply", or even in a "for loop", the warning messages are silenced. I know that some warnings exist because I have come across them when fitting the model to single genes. Sometimes there seems to be a problem with the convergence and some other times about a parameter value that should be changed, as far as I remember.

I have tried to dump the screen output to a file, but it came out empty, I have also tried things like "withCallingHandlers", "tryCatch" and other things, but the result is always the same: nothing at all.

Is there any option that can be enabled/disabled in the inla() call that will allow me to store these messages? It would be really useful to see whether there is a pattern in the problematic genes and whether something can be done about it.

Thank you very much for your help.

Best regards,
Maria

if you do

r = inla(...)

then r$logfile

contains a copy of all the output, including warnings. do you intend to
check for warnings and if so, rerun that example or skip it or
something? there are ways to check that the results obtained pass the
'internal checks'.

I'm refering to the latest testing-version.

let

r = inla(...)

then if

r$ok == TRUE

then r contains all the results that was intended, hence if r$ok==FALSE
then the inla-program has crashed.

if r$mode$mode.status == 0 then the posterior mode of the
hyperparameters pass all the internal checks. depending on usage, small
values here are usually ok not always.

the mode$mode.status number is the number of check's not passed, hence
higher is worse. an exception is if the -Hessian is not SPD, for which
its add 1000 to mode$mode.status (as this is pretty serious, and would
require a rerun to located the posterior mode).
